chapter.title: Exhaustive Answer Keys and Pedagogical Explanations
chapter.description: The single consolidated answer key for the whole book. It contains the answers and bilingual pedagogical explanations for exercises from Chapters 1 to 6, with the Chapter 4 speaking and Chapter 6 open-response tasks handled according to the source.
learning_objectives: Check answers for exercises from Chapters 1 to 6 in one authoritative location.
Understand why each answer is correct through English explanations.
Understand the same grammar, lexical, collocation, and register points through Bangla explanations.
Identify why common student answers fail and avoid repeating the same errors.
Use the Chapter 4 speaking-drill judging criteria and Chapter 6 self-assessment criteria.

blocks.title: Chapter 7 introduction
blocks.content:
Chapter 7: Exhaustive Answer Keys and Pedagogical Explanations
(Part 1 of 2)
This chapter is the single, definitive answer key for the whole book. Every exercise in Chapters 1
to 6 is answered here in full, and each answer is explained twice: once in English and once in
Bangla, so the reasoning is clear whichever language you think in. The explanations focus on
two things the examiner cares about: why the correct answer is correct, and why the
common student version fails. Understanding the second is what stops an error from
coming back.
Part 1, this file, covers Chapters 1, 2, and 3. Part 2 covers Chapters 4, 5, and 6.
The in-chapter keys can stay as a quick self-check while you study, but this chapter is the
authoritative version.

blocks.title: Chapter 1: The Bangladeshi L1 Interference Fixer
blocks.content:
Chapter 1: The Bangladeshi L1 Interference Fixer
Exercise 1.1 · Spot the L1 Error
1. Scientists are still discussing the real causes of climate change. - Why: discuss is transitive
and takes its object directly; discuss about doubles a meaning the verb already carries. - বাংলা:
discuss-এর পরে about বসে না, কারণ “আলোচনা করা”-র object সরাসরি বসে; “নিয়ে/সম্পর্কে ” verb-এর ভেতরেই
আছে।
2. This report comprises five main sections and a short appendix. (or consists of) - Why:
comprise takes no of; the of belongs only to consist of and be composed of. - বাংলা: comprise-এর
পরে of বসে না; of বসে শুধু consist of-এর সাথে।
3. My elder brother is senior to me by four years. - Why: Latin-origin comparatives (senior,
junior, superior, prior) take to, never than. - বাংলা: senior/junior জাতীয় শব্দের পরে than নয়, to বসে।

4. My sister is married to a civil engineer from Khulna. - Why: the fixed collocation is married
to; with is used for doing something alongside a person, not for the marriage bond. - বাংলা: বিয়ের
ক্ষেত্রে married to হয়, married with নয়।
5. I have been staying in this hostel since my first year, and I still live here. - Why: a situation
that began in the past and continues now needs the present perfect, not the present continuous.
- বাংলা: অতীতে শুরু হয়ে এখনও চলছে এমন অবস্থায় present continuous নয়, present perfect লাগে।
6. The counsellor gave me two very useful pieces of advice about choosing a subject. - Why:
advice is uncountable, so it cannot take a plural -s; to count it, use pieces of advice. - বাংলা: advice
অগণনীয়, তাই plural -s বসে না; গুনতে হলে pieces of advice বলুন।
7. Everyone in our study group is preparing hard for the mock test. - Why: everyone is
grammatically singular, however many people it refers to; the phrase in our study group does
not change the verb. - বাংলা: everyone সবসময় singular, তাই verb হবে is।
8. Despite the heavy workload, she submitted every assignment on time. - Why: despite takes
no of; only in spite of keeps the of. - বাংলা: despite-এর পরে of বসে না; of বসে শুধু in spite of-এ।
9. In my opinion, public libraries should stay open late into the evening. - Why: according to
introduces an external source, not your own view; use in my opinion for yourself. - বাংলা:
according to বাইরের সূত্র বোঝায়; নিজের মত বোঝাতে in my opinion বলুন।
10. The number of private cars on the road is rising sharply each year. - Why: the true subject
is number (singular); the number of always takes a singular verb. - বাংলা: এখানে subject হলো
number (singular), তাই the number of-এর পরে verb singular হয়।
11. It is difficult for many workers to cope with rapid technological change. - Why: the verb is
cope with; the extra up is a regional habit with no basis in the phrase. - বাংলা: সঠিক হলো cope with;
cope up with আঞ্চলিক ভু ল, up বসে না।
12. Please turn on the light; the room is too dark to read in. - Why: lights and devices are
turned on or off; open/close apply to doors and windows. - বাংলা: বাতির জন্য turn on/off হয়;
open/close দরজা-জানালার জন্য।
13. We reached the examination hall twenty minutes before it started. (or arrived at) - Why:
reach is transitive and takes no preposition; arrive takes at or in. - বাংলা: reach-এর পরে to বসে না;
বিকল্পে arrive at বলা যায়।
14. Most students prefer group study to studying alone at home. - Why: prefer pairs with to, not
than; keep both options in the same form (study to studying). - বাংলা: prefer-এর পরে than নয়, to
বসে।
15. After completing his research, he returned to his home country. - Why: return already
means “go back,” so back is redundant. - বাংলা: return-এর মধ্যেই “ফিরে যাওয়া” অর্থ আছে, তাই back
অপ্রয়োজনীয়।

Exercise 1.2 · Bangla to Band 9 Translation Challenge
Model answers with the trap each one targets.

1. Most people believe that technology has made our daily lives much easier. - Trap: maximum
for most; use the present perfect for a change with present relevance. - বাংলা: maximum নয়, most;
বর্তমান-প্রাসঙ্গিক পরিবর্তনে present perfect।
2. Despite the traffic congestion, most city dwellers still prefer to use private cars. - Trap:
despite of; prefer … to. - বাংলা: despite-এ of নেই; prefer to।
3. In my opinion, the government should invest more heavily in the education sector. - Trap:
according to me; invest in. - বাংলা: according to me নয়, in my opinion; invest in।
4. I have been researching this subject since 2018. - Trap: present continuous with since;
research is transitive, no about. - বাংলা: since থাকলে present perfect continuous; research about
নয়।
5. Pollution poses a serious threat to public health. - Trap: use the precise collocation pose a
threat to rather than a vague verb. - বাংলা: অস্পষ্ট শব্দের বদলে সঠিক collocation pose a threat to।
6. It is essential to create employment opportunities for the younger generation. - Trap: formal
it is essential to; natural phrase the younger generation. - বাংলা: আনুষ্ঠানিক it is essential to; the
younger generation।
7. Although many students are good at English, they fail to perform well in the exam. - Trap:
good in to good at; although with a full clause. - বাংলা: good in নয়, good at; পূর্ণ clause-এ although।
8. I hope to build my own company one day. - Trap: natural build/establish a company and
hope to, not a word-for-word translation. - বাংলা: শব্দে-শব্দে অনুবাদ নয়; স্বাভাবিক hope to build my own
company।
9. Eradicating poverty is the biggest challenge for any developing nation. - Trap: eradicate
upgrades remove; a gerund subject. - বাংলা: remove-এর উন্নত রূপ eradicate; gerund দিয়ে subject।
10. If the government enacted stricter laws, the crime rate would decrease. - Trap: second
conditional (past after if, would in the result); the crime rate, not the rate of crime are. - বাংলা:
second conditional; if-এর পরে past, ফলাংশে would।

blocks.title: Chapter 2: The Band Upgrade Matrix
blocks.content:
Chapter 2: The Band Upgrade Matrix
Exercise 2.1 · Lexical Upgrade Drill
Model rewrites, with the core upgrade named. Other natural versions are valid.
1. Pollution is a pressing issue that the government must tackle urgently. (big problem to
pressing issue; solve fast to tackle urgently.) 2. The internet is highly beneficial because it
enables students to learn far more efficiently. (good thing to highly beneficial.) 3. Many people
believe that financial security is essential to a contented life. (money/important/happy all
upgraded.) 4. Climate change is a grave threat that affects numerous countries. (very dangerous
thing to grave threat.) 5. Emerging technologies have transformed our lives and simplified
countless tasks. (new technology/changed upgraded.) 6. Affluent nations should support
developing countries in reducing poverty. (rich/poor countries/help upgraded.) 7. Tourism is

beneficial to the economy, yet it can also be detrimental to the environment. (good for/bad for
upgraded.) 8. Education is a crucial means of addressing unemployment. (very important
way/solve the problem of upgraded.) 9. Large cities suffer from heavy traffic congestion, which
gives rise to numerous difficulties. (big/a lot of traffic/causes many problems upgraded.) 10.
Social media is immensely popular among young people and is reshaping the way they
communicate. (very famous thing/talk upgraded.)
  •     Why (general): each vague word (big, good, thing, help, change) is replaced by a precise,
        collocation-appropriate one, which is what lifts Lexical Resource from Band 6 to Band 8.
  •     বাংলা: প্রতিটি অস্পষ্ট শব্দ (big, good, thing) সঠিক ও collocation-উপযোগী শব্দে বদলে দিলে Lexical
        Resource বাড়ে ।

Exercise 2.2 · Context Match
1. eradicate. Why: it means remove completely; alleviate only means ease, so it fails here. বাংলা:
eradicate = সম্পূর্ণ নির্মূল; alleviate = শুধু লাঘব, তাই ভু ল। 2. alleviate. Why: it eases pain that already
exists; eradicate is ruled out by “cannot be cured.” বাংলা: বিদ্যমান কষ্ট লাঘব করা; নির্মূল নয়। 3. mitigate.
Why: mitigate the damage means reduce its severity; the fixed collocation. বাংলা: ক্ষতির তীব্রতা
কমানো; নির্দিষ্ট collocation। 4. soared. Why: soar means a large, rapid rise, matching “dramatically.”
বাংলা: soar = দ্রুত বড় উত্থান, “dramatically”-র সাথে মানানসই। 5. declined. Why: a gradual fall fits
“steadily”; soared would contradict it. বাংলা: “steadily”-র সাথে ধীরে হ্রাস; soared বিপরীত। 6. vital.
Why: means essential; trivial is the opposite and contradicts the sentence. বাংলা: vital = অত্যাবশ্যক;
trivial বিপরীত। 7. revolutionised. Why: a radical, lasting change fits the printing press. বাংলা: আমূল
স্থায়ী পরিবর্তন বোঝায়। 8. trigger. Why: it means set off a harmful event; mitigate would reverse the
meaning. বাংলা: ক্ষতিকর কিছু ঘটানো; mitigate বিপরীত। 9. highlights. Why: to draw attention to a
finding; conceals is the opposite. বাংলা: গুরুত্ব তুলে ধরা; conceals বিপরীত। 10. affluent. Why: means
wealthy; impoverished means the opposite. বাংলা: affluent = ধনী; impoverished বিপরীত। 11.
diminish. Why: to make less; worsen contradicts the benefit of exercise. বাংলা: কমানো; worsen
বিপরীত। 12. reshape. Why: to change significantly; preserve means keep unchanged. বাংলা: বড়
পরিবর্তন; preserve বিপরীত। 13. generated. Why: means produced or caused; resolved means settled,
the opposite. বাংলা: সৃষ্টি করা; resolved বিপরীত। 14. alleviate. Why: to ease suffering; aggravate
means make it worse. বাংলা: কষ্ট লাঘব; aggravate বিপরীত। 15. crucial. Why: means very important;
trivial is the opposite. বাংলা: crucial = অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ; trivial বিপরীত।

blocks.title: Chapter 3: Complete Verb Conjugations and Formal Transitions
blocks.content:
Chapter 3: Complete Verb Conjugations and Formal Transitions
Exercise 3.1 · Verb Form and Collocation Drill
1. grown. Why: present perfect needs has + V3; grow is irregular (grew, grown). বাংলা: present
perfect-এ has + V3; grow-এর V3 grown। 2. to rise / rising. Why: continue accepts both the
infinitive and the -ing form. বাংলা: continue-এর পরে to + verb বা -ing দুটোই চলে। 3. on. Why: depend
on is the fixed collocation. বাংলা: depend on। 4. from. Why: benefit from. বাংলা: benefit from। 5.
peaked. Why: simple past for a finished time range. বাংলা: নির্দিষ্ট অতীত সময়ে simple past। 6. risen.
Why: present perfect (has risen); rise is intransitive, so no object. বাংলা: present perfect has risen;
rise intransitive। 7. in. Why: invest in. বাংলা: invest in। 8. eradicated. Why: passive voice needs

was + V3. বাংলা: passive-এ was + V3। 9. undermine. Why: the base form follows the modal may.
বাংলা: modal may-এর পরে base form। 10. focuses. Why: present simple, third person singular (the
report focuses on). বাংলা: third person singular-এ focuses। 11. fallen. Why: past perfect needs had
+ V3; fall is irregular (fell, fallen). বাংলা: past perfect-এ had + V3। 12. to. Why: contribute to. বাংলা:
contribute to। 13. deter … from. Why: base form after can; the structure is deter someone from
doing. বাংলা: can-এর পরে base; deter … from। 14. investing. Why: present perfect continuous
needs has been + V4. বাংলা: present perfect continuous-এ has been + -ing। 15. from. Why: result
from points to a cause; result in points to a consequence. বাংলা: কারণ বোঝাতে result from; ফল বোঝাতে
result in। 16. replacing. Why: present continuous needs are + V4. বাংলা: present continuous-এ
are + -ing। 17. designed … enhance. Why: passive is designed; base form after to. বাংলা: passive is
designed; to-এর পরে base। 18. adapt … to. Why: base form after must; adapt to. বাংলা: must-এর পরে
base; adapt to। 19. risen. Why: present perfect (have risen). বাংলা: present perfect have risen।
20. provided … with. Why: present perfect has provided; provide someone with something. বাংলা:
provide … with।

Exercise 3.2 · Cohesive Device Transformation
Model rewrite:
      Online education has grown enormously in popularity, largely because it is cheaper
      than traditional classes and allows students to study from home. Notwithstanding
      these advantages, it carries certain drawbacks. To begin with, there is far less
      interaction with teachers. Moreover, many learners lack the self-discipline that
      independent study demands; consequently, a significant proportion fail to complete
      their courses. Online education is therefore undeniably useful, yet it cannot fully
      replace the classroom.
  •     Why: because correctly introduces a full clause, while Notwithstanding is correctly
        followed by a noun phrase (these advantages), not a clause; the semicolon before
        consequently joins two related clauses; no device is repeated, so the cohesion is varied
        rather than mechanical.
  •     বাংলা: because-এর পরে পূর্ণ clause; Notwithstanding-এর পরে noun phrase (clause নয়);
        consequently-র আগে semicolon; একই linker বারবার না বসিয়ে বৈচিত্র্য রাখা হয়েছে, যা উচ্চ band-এর
        লক্ষণ।


End of Chapter 7, Part 1. Part 2 consolidates the keys for Chapters 4, 5, and 6.

blocks.title: Chapter 7 Part 2 introduction
blocks.content:
Chapter 7: Exhaustive Answer Keys and Pedagogical Explanations
(Part 2 of 2)
This file completes the master key, covering Chapters 4, 5, and 6. Match and completion
answers are given in full for every topic; each carries a bilingual note on the collocation or rule
being tested. The Speaking drills in Chapter 4 and the essay and speaking models in Chapter 6
are open-response tasks whose full model answers appear in their own chapter files, so here

blocks.title: Chapter 4: Topic-Based Lexical Mastery
blocks.content:
they are cross-referenced rather than reprinted, with a bilingual note on how to judge your
own version.



Chapter 4: Topic-Based Lexical Mastery
For each topic: the Match answers, the Completion answers, and a bilingual note. The
Speaking simulation answers are open; a model for the first question of each topic appears in
the relevant Chapter 4 batch file.

Batch 1
Topic 1 · Environment. Match: 1-e, 2-a, 3-j, 4-b, 5-i, 6-c, 7-h, 8-d, 9-g, 10-f. Completion: 1 strike,
2 pollutants, 3 renewable, 4 irreversible, 5 footprint. - Why: the completion items test fixed
collocations (strike a balance, renewable energy, irreversible damage, carbon footprint), not just
meaning. - বাংলা: completion অংশে অর্থ নয়, নির্দিষ্ট collocation পরীক্ষা করা হয়েছে (strike a balance, carbon
footprint)।
Topic 2 · Education. Match: 1-d, 2-a, 3-i, 4-e, 5-f, 6-g, 7-c, 8-h, 9-b, 10-j. Completion: 1 education,
2 bridge, 3 critical, 4 lifelong, 5 foundation. - Why: bridge the skills gap, critical thinking, lifelong
learning, and lay the foundation are all set academic phrases. - বাংলা: critical thinking, lifelong
learning ইত্যাদি নির্দিষ্ট academic phrase।
Topic 3 · Technology. Match: 1-b, 2-c, 3-d, 4-e, 5-h, 6-i, 7-a, 8-f, 9-g, 10-j. Completion: 1
transformed (or revolutionised), 2 automation, 3 digital, 4 concerns, 5 automated. - Why:
transform the way, bridge the digital divide, and raise ethical concerns are the target
collocations. - বাংলা: digital divide, ethical concerns ইত্যাদি লক্ষ্য collocation।
Topic 4 · Health. Match: 1-a, 2-c, 3-e, 4-d, 5-f, 6-g, 7-h, 8-i, 9-j, 10-b. Completion: 1 balanced, 2
strain, 3 toll, 4 lifestyle, 5 alleviate. - Why: a balanced diet, place a strain on, take a toll on, and a
healthy lifestyle are fixed pairings. - বাংলা: balanced diet, take a toll on নির্দিষ্ট শব্দ-জোড় ।
Topic 5 · Crime. Match: 1-c, 2-f, 3-b, 4-a, 5-d, 6-g, 7-i, 8-j, 9-e, 10-h. Completion: 1 deterrent, 2
rehabilitate, 3 causes, 4 impose, 5 reintegrate. - Why: act as a deterrent, address the root causes,
impose penalties, reintegrate into society are the essay phrases. - বাংলা: root causes, reintegrate
into society ইত্যাদি রচনার phrase।

Batch 2
Topic 6 · Globalisation. Match: 1-c, 2-i, 3-b, 4-f, 5-e, 6-g, 7-d, 8-j, 9-a, 10-h. Completion: 1 erode,
2 diversity, 3 assimilate (or integrate), 4 barriers, 5 risk. - Why: erode values, cultural diversity,
break down barriers, at the risk of are the targets. - বাংলা: cultural diversity, break down barriers
লক্ষ্য collocation।
Topic 7 · Urbanisation. Match: 1-c, 2-b, 3-a, 4-d, 5-f, 6-e, 7-g, 8-h, 9-i, 10-j. Completion: 1
urbanisation, 2 affordable, 3 congestion, 4 cope, 5 planning. - Why: affordable housing, traffic
congestion, cope with growth, urban planning are set phrases. - বাংলা: affordable housing, urban
planning নির্দিষ্ট phrase।

Topic 8 · Business and Economy. Match: 1-c, 2-e, 3-a, 4-d, 5-b, 6-h, 7-f, 8-g, 9-j, 10-i.
Completion: 1 stimulate, 2 widen, 3 inflation, 4 create, 5 economy. - Why: stimulate growth,
widen the gap, create opportunities, booming economy are the collocations. - বাংলা: stimulate
growth, widen the gap লক্ষ্য collocation।
Topic 9 · Arts and Heritage. Match: 1-c, 2-a, 3-b, 4-d, 5-e, 6-g, 7-f, 8-h, 9-i, 10-j. Completion: 1
generations, 2 identity, 3 down, 4 traditions, 5 reflects. - Why: preserve for future generations, a
sense of identity, pass down, keep traditions alive are the phrases. - বাংলা: pass down, keep
traditions alive নির্দিষ্ট phrase।
Topic 10 · Media and Advertising. Match: 1-b, 2-c, 3-d, 4-f, 5-h, 6-a, 7-e, 8-g, 9-j, 10-i.
Completion: 1 shape, 2 manipulate, 3 spread, 4 account, 5 advertising. - Why: shape public
opinion, manipulate behaviour, spread misinformation, hold to account are the targets. - বাংলা:
shape public opinion, spread misinformation লক্ষ্য collocation।

Batch 3
Topic 11 · Government and Public Spending. Match: 1-c, 2-e, 3-b, 4-f, 5-d, 6-a, 7-h, 8-g, 9-i, 10-
j. Completion: 1 allocate, 2 accountable, 3 services, 4 red, 5 policy. - Why: allocate resources, hold
accountable, public services, red tape, fiscal policy are the collocations. - বাংলা: allocate resources,
red tape নির্দিষ্ট collocation।
Topic 12 · Transportation. Match: 1-c, 2-a, 3-d, 4-b, 5-e, 6-f, 7-g, 8-h, 9-i, 10-j. Completion: 1
invest, 2 discourage, 3 reduce, 4 transit (or mass transit), 5 connectivity. - Why: invest in public
transport, discourage car use, reduce emissions, improve connectivity are the phrases. - বাংলা:
invest in public transport, reduce emissions লক্ষ্য phrase।
Topic 13 · Youth and Family. Match: 1-b, 2-a, 3-f, 4-d, 5-e, 6-g, 7-h, 8-i, 9-j, 10-c. Completion: 1
gap, 2 values, 3 balance, 4 shape, 5 time. - Why: bridge the generation gap, instil values, strike a
balance, shape character, quality time are the targets. - বাংলা: generation gap, quality time নির্দিষ্ট
collocation।
Topic 14 · Scientific Research. Match: 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-e, 5-c, 6-h, 7-i, 8-j, 9-f, 10-g. Completion: 1
boundaries, 2 rigorous, 3 questions (or concerns), 4 funding, 5 pave. - Why: push the
boundaries, rigorous testing, ethical questions, allocate funding, pave the way are the phrases. -
বাংলা: push the boundaries, pave the way লক্ষ্য phrase।
Topic 15 · Tourism. Match: 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d, 5-f, 6-e, 7-h, 8-i, 9-j, 10-g. Completion: 1 boost, 2
broaden, 3 strain, 4 preserve, 5 cultural. - Why: boost the local economy, broaden one’s horizons,
put a strain on, preserve attractions, cultural understanding are the targets. - বাংলা: boost the
local economy, broaden one’s horizons নির্দিষ্ট collocation।

blocks.title: Chapter 5: Idioms and Phrasal Verbs
blocks.content:
Judging the Speaking drills. For every Part 3 question, a correct answer is any natural, error-
free response that uses at least one target collocation and, where suitable, one idiom, and
answers the question directly. Full model answers for all three questions of every topic are
given in the Chapter 4 batch files. - বাংলা: Speaking drill-এ সঠিক উত্তর হলো এমন যেকোনো স্বাভাবিক, নির্ভুল
উত্তর যা প্রশ্নের জবাব দেয় এবং অন্তত একটি লক্ষ্য collocation ব্যবহার করে।

Chapter 5: Idioms and Phrasal Verbs
Exercise 5.1 · Register and Style Sort
The answer is W (appropriate for Task 2) or S (Speaking only). For each S, a formal rewrite is
given.
1. S. These days, many children spend excessive time on their smartphones. (a lot of kids, glued
to, around the clock are all informal.) 2. W. Appropriate. 3. S. The government must take
decisive action on pollution. (get its act together is informal.) 4. W. Appropriate. 5. S.
Ultimately, the responsibility lies with the individual. (at the end of the day, it is up to are
informal.) 6. W. Appropriate. 7. S. Fast food is both overpriced and detrimental to health. (a rip-
off, bad for you are informal.) 8. W. Appropriate. 9. S. A significant proportion of people believe
that exams are unfair. (loads of, reckon are informal.) 10. W. Appropriate. 11. S. Many young
people today show little interest in tradition. (could not care less is informal.) 12. W.
Appropriate. 13. S. Social media brings both clear benefits and serious drawbacks. (to be honest
is a spoken hedge.) 14. W. Appropriate. 15. S. In my view, the current system is deeply flawed.
(if you ask me, a mess are informal.) 16. W. Appropriate. 17. S. Tourism can boost the economy,
though it brings mixed outcomes. (a bit of a mixed bag is informal.) 18. W. Appropriate. 19. S.
The wealthy should contribute more in taxes. (cough up is informal.) 20. W. Appropriate.
  •    Why: informal idioms and phrasal verbs lower the register of a Task 2 essay, which
       pulls Lexical Resource down even when the vocabulary is otherwise rich. The formal
       rewrites preserve the meaning while restoring academic tone.
  •    বাংলা: অনানুষ্ঠানিক idiom ও phrasal verb Task 2 রচনার register নামিয়ে দেয়, ফলে Lexical Resource
       কমে; আনুষ্ঠানিক রূপান্তরে অর্থ ঠিক রেখে academic সুর ফিরে আসে।

Exercise 5.2 · Idiom Substitution
1. on cloud nine (not “cloud seven”). বাংলা: সঠিক রূপ on cloud nine। 2. a piece of cake (not “a piece
of pie”). বাংলা: সঠিক idiom a piece of cake। 3. a fish out of water (not “a fish in the water”; it
means uncomfortable in a new situation). বাংলা: a fish out of water মানে নতুন পরিবেশে অস্বস্তি; “in the
water” বললে অর্থ উল্টে যায়। 4. a stone’s throw from (not “a stone throw”). বাংলা: সঠিক রূপ a stone’s
throw from (possessive)। 5. a steep learning curve (not “a steep hill”). বাংলা: সঠিক idiom a steep

blocks.title: Chapter 6: Full Workbook and Self-Assessment
blocks.content:
learning curve। 6. kill two birds with one stone (not “in one stone”). বাংলা: সঠিক রূপ with one
stone। 7. back to the drawing board (not “the painting board”). বাংলা: সঠিক idiom back to the
drawing board। 8. at the drop of a hat (not “the drop of the hat”). বাংলা: সঠিক রূপ at the drop of a
hat।



Chapter 6: Full Workbook and Self-Assessment
Section 1 · Sentence Transformations (Band 9 models)
  1. In the modern era, technology plays an indispensable role in our daily lives.
  2. Many people believe that wealth is the key to happiness.
  3. Pollution poses a serious threat to public health.
  4. The government should allocate greater funding to education.

  5.    A significant proportion of students go abroad in pursuit of well-paid employment.
  6.    Deforestation has a detrimental effect on the environment.
  7.    Children spend excessive time on their phones, which can be detrimental to their
        development.
  8.    An efficient public transport system can substantially reduce urban traffic congestion.
  9.    Examinations place considerable pressure on students.
  10.   Tourism makes a substantial contribution to a nation’s economy.
  11.   Disadvantaged people often lack access to adequate healthcare.
  12.   Social media has fundamentally transformed the way people communicate.
  13.   Although fast food is popular, it gives rise to numerous health problems.
  14.   Large corporations should do more to protect the environment.
  15.   A command of English is crucial for securing well-paid employment.
  16.   The gap between rich and poor continues to widen.
  17.   Excessive television viewing is an unproductive use of children’s time.
  18.   Crime often stems from unemployment and a lack of opportunity.
  19.   Long-standing traditions are gradually disappearing as a result of modern life.
  20.   Renewable energy is a cleaner and more sustainable alternative to fossil fuels.
  •     Why: each transformation replaces an overused word with a precise one, folds two weak
        clauses into one controlled sentence, and swaps a basic linker for an accurate cohesive
        device. That combination of precision and control is what moves a sentence from Band 6
        to Band 9.
  •     বাংলা: প্রতিটি রূপান্তরে অতিব্যবহৃত শব্দ সঠিক শব্দে বদলানো হয়েছে, দুর্বল clause একত্র করে নিয়ন্ত্রিত বাক্য বানানো
        হয়েছে এবং সাধারণ linker সঠিক cohesive device-এ পরিণত হয়েছে; এই নির্ভুলতা ও নিয়ন্ত্রণই Band 6 থেকে
        Band 9-এ নিয়ে যায়।

Section 2 · Essay Rewrites
Full model rewrites for all five essays appear in Chapter 6, Part 1. Compare your version
against the model and check, paragraph by paragraph, whether you applied the following. -
Why (the upgrade checklist): remove first-language slips (I am agree, give importance on,
discuss about); replace overused words (big, good, bad, a lot of, thing) with precise choices;
swap basic linkers (but, so, also) for cohesive devices (Nevertheless, Consequently,
Furthermore); and add at least one formal collocation per paragraph (reap the benefits, strike a
balance, pose a serious threat to). - বাংলা: L1 ভু ল সরান (I am agree, discuss about); অতিব্যবহৃত শব্দ সঠিক
শব্দে বদলান; সাধারণ linker-এর বদলে cohesive device দিন; প্রতিটি অনুচ্ছেদে অন্তত একটি আনুষ্ঠানিক collocation
যোগ করুন। পূর্ণ মডেল রচনা Chapter 6, Part 1-এ আছে।

Speaking Simulations (Chapter 6, Part 2)
The five simulations are open-response tasks; full model long-turn and Part 3 answers, with a
lexical analysis of each, appear in Chapter 6, Part 2. Judge your own attempt on three points. -

blocks.title: Chapter 7 closing
blocks.content:
Why: did you speak for the full two minutes without drying up; did you use natural idioms (not
essay language) in Part 2; and did you shift toward argument collocations in Part 3? Those
three are exactly what a Speaking examiner rewards under Lexical Resource. - বাংলা: পুরো দুই মিনিট

থেমে না গিয়ে বলতে পেরেছেন কি; Part 2-এ স্বাভাবিক idiom (রচনার ভাষা নয়) ব্যবহার করেছেন কি; Part 3-এ যুক্তির
collocation-এ গেছেন কি; এই তিনটিই Speaking examiner-এর মূল্যায়নের ভিত্তি।



The book is complete
All seven chapters and the front matter are now written: the diagnostic and scoring blueprint,
the L1 interference fixer, the band upgrade matrix, the verb and transition reference, the fifteen
topic bundles, the strict idiom separation, the full workbook, and this consolidated key. Worked
in order, with a pen, and returned to whenever an error recurs, this material takes a disciplined
HSC-level learner from vague, translated English to the precise, register-aware language that
the higher bands reward. Range and accuracy grow together, and together they move the band.
A note on assembling the manuscript. The book has been delivered as eleven Markdown
files (front matter, Chapters 1 to 3, Chapter 4 in three batches, Chapter 5, Chapter 6 in two parts,
and Chapter 7 in two parts). To publish, they can be concatenated in that order into a single
document, and the in-chapter answer keys can either be removed in favour of this Chapter 7 or
kept as a study convenience. If a Word or PDF edition is wanted, the combined Markdown can
be converted directly.
End of Chapter 7, and of Zero to Band 9.

answer_key.note: Chapter 7 is the definitive consolidated answer key. The Appendix/Word Bank is deliberately excluded from this JSON.

source_text:
Chapter 7: Exhaustive Answer Keys and Pedagogical Explanations
(Part 1 of 2)
This chapter is the single, definitive answer key for the whole book. Every exercise in Chapters 1
to 6 is answered here in full, and each answer is explained twice: once in English and once in
Bangla, so the reasoning is clear whichever language you think in. The explanations focus on
two things the examiner cares about: why the correct answer is correct, and why the
common student version fails. Understanding the second is what stops an error from
coming back.
Part 1, this file, covers Chapters 1, 2, and 3. Part 2 covers Chapters 4, 5, and 6.
The in-chapter keys can stay as a quick self-check while you study, but this chapter is the
authoritative version.



Chapter 1: The Bangladeshi L1 Interference Fixer
Exercise 1.1 · Spot the L1 Error
1. Scientists are still discussing the real causes of climate change. - Why: discuss is transitive
and takes its object directly; discuss about doubles a meaning the verb already carries. - বাংলা:
discuss-এর পরে about বসে না, কারণ “আলোচনা করা”-র object সরাসরি বসে; “নিয়ে/সম্পর্কে ” verb-এর ভেতরেই
আছে।
2. This report comprises five main sections and a short appendix. (or consists of) - Why:
comprise takes no of; the of belongs only to consist of and be composed of. - বাংলা: comprise-এর
পরে of বসে না; of বসে শুধু consist of-এর সাথে।
3. My elder brother is senior to me by four years. - Why: Latin-origin comparatives (senior,
junior, superior, prior) take to, never than. - বাংলা: senior/junior জাতীয় শব্দের পরে than নয়, to বসে।

4. My sister is married to a civil engineer from Khulna. - Why: the fixed collocation is married
to; with is used for doing something alongside a person, not for the marriage bond. - বাংলা: বিয়ের
ক্ষেত্রে married to হয়, married with নয়।
5. I have been staying in this hostel since my first year, and I still live here. - Why: a situation
that began in the past and continues now needs the present perfect, not the present continuous.
- বাংলা: অতীতে শুরু হয়ে এখনও চলছে এমন অবস্থায় present continuous নয়, present perfect লাগে।
6. The counsellor gave me two very useful pieces of advice about choosing a subject. - Why:
advice is uncountable, so it cannot take a plural -s; to count it, use pieces of advice. - বাংলা: advice
অগণনীয়, তাই plural -s বসে না; গুনতে হলে pieces of advice বলুন।
7. Everyone in our study group is preparing hard for the mock test. - Why: everyone is
grammatically singular, however many people it refers to; the phrase in our study group does
not change the verb. - বাংলা: everyone সবসময় singular, তাই verb হবে is।
8. Despite the heavy workload, she submitted every assignment on time. - Why: despite takes
no of; only in spite of keeps the of. - বাংলা: despite-এর পরে of বসে না; of বসে শুধু in spite of-এ।
9. In my opinion, public libraries should stay open late into the evening. - Why: according to
introduces an external source, not your own view; use in my opinion for yourself. - বাংলা:
according to বাইরের সূত্র বোঝায়; নিজের মত বোঝাতে in my opinion বলুন।
10. The number of private cars on the road is rising sharply each year. - Why: the true subject
is number (singular); the number of always takes a singular verb. - বাংলা: এখানে subject হলো
number (singular), তাই the number of-এর পরে verb singular হয়।
11. It is difficult for many workers to cope with rapid technological change. - Why: the verb is
cope with; the extra up is a regional habit with no basis in the phrase. - বাংলা: সঠিক হলো cope with;
cope up with আঞ্চলিক ভু ল, up বসে না।
12. Please turn on the light; the room is too dark to read in. - Why: lights and devices are
turned on or off; open/close apply to doors and windows. - বাংলা: বাতির জন্য turn on/off হয়;
open/close দরজা-জানালার জন্য।
13. We reached the examination hall twenty minutes before it started. (or arrived at) - Why:
reach is transitive and takes no preposition; arrive takes at or in. - বাংলা: reach-এর পরে to বসে না;
বিকল্পে arrive at বলা যায়।
14. Most students prefer group study to studying alone at home. - Why: prefer pairs with to, not
than; keep both options in the same form (study to studying). - বাংলা: prefer-এর পরে than নয়, to
বসে।
15. After completing his research, he returned to his home country. - Why: return already
means “go back,” so back is redundant. - বাংলা: return-এর মধ্যেই “ফিরে যাওয়া” অর্থ আছে, তাই back
অপ্রয়োজনীয়।

Exercise 1.2 · Bangla to Band 9 Translation Challenge
Model answers with the trap each one targets.

1. Most people believe that technology has made our daily lives much easier. - Trap: maximum
for most; use the present perfect for a change with present relevance. - বাংলা: maximum নয়, most;
বর্তমান-প্রাসঙ্গিক পরিবর্তনে present perfect।
2. Despite the traffic congestion, most city dwellers still prefer to use private cars. - Trap:
despite of; prefer … to. - বাংলা: despite-এ of নেই; prefer to।
3. In my opinion, the government should invest more heavily in the education sector. - Trap:
according to me; invest in. - বাংলা: according to me নয়, in my opinion; invest in।
4. I have been researching this subject since 2018. - Trap: present continuous with since;
research is transitive, no about. - বাংলা: since থাকলে present perfect continuous; research about
নয়।
5. Pollution poses a serious threat to public health. - Trap: use the precise collocation pose a
threat to rather than a vague verb. - বাংলা: অস্পষ্ট শব্দের বদলে সঠিক collocation pose a threat to।
6. It is essential to create employment opportunities for the younger generation. - Trap: formal
it is essential to; natural phrase the younger generation. - বাংলা: আনুষ্ঠানিক it is essential to; the
younger generation।
7. Although many students are good at English, they fail to perform well in the exam. - Trap:
good in to good at; although with a full clause. - বাংলা: good in নয়, good at; পূর্ণ clause-এ although।
8. I hope to build my own company one day. - Trap: natural build/establish a company and
hope to, not a word-for-word translation. - বাংলা: শব্দে-শব্দে অনুবাদ নয়; স্বাভাবিক hope to build my own
company।
9. Eradicating poverty is the biggest challenge for any developing nation. - Trap: eradicate
upgrades remove; a gerund subject. - বাংলা: remove-এর উন্নত রূপ eradicate; gerund দিয়ে subject।
10. If the government enacted stricter laws, the crime rate would decrease. - Trap: second
conditional (past after if, would in the result); the crime rate, not the rate of crime are. - বাংলা:
second conditional; if-এর পরে past, ফলাংশে would।



Chapter 2: The Band Upgrade Matrix
Exercise 2.1 · Lexical Upgrade Drill
Model rewrites, with the core upgrade named. Other natural versions are valid.
1. Pollution is a pressing issue that the government must tackle urgently. (big problem to
pressing issue; solve fast to tackle urgently.) 2. The internet is highly beneficial because it
enables students to learn far more efficiently. (good thing to highly beneficial.) 3. Many people
believe that financial security is essential to a contented life. (money/important/happy all
upgraded.) 4. Climate change is a grave threat that affects numerous countries. (very dangerous
thing to grave threat.) 5. Emerging technologies have transformed our lives and simplified
countless tasks. (new technology/changed upgraded.) 6. Affluent nations should support
developing countries in reducing poverty. (rich/poor countries/help upgraded.) 7. Tourism is

beneficial to the economy, yet it can also be detrimental to the environment. (good for/bad for
upgraded.) 8. Education is a crucial means of addressing unemployment. (very important
way/solve the problem of upgraded.) 9. Large cities suffer from heavy traffic congestion, which
gives rise to numerous difficulties. (big/a lot of traffic/causes many problems upgraded.) 10.
Social media is immensely popular among young people and is reshaping the way they
communicate. (very famous thing/talk upgraded.)
  •     Why (general): each vague word (big, good, thing, help, change) is replaced by a precise,
        collocation-appropriate one, which is what lifts Lexical Resource from Band 6 to Band 8.
  •     বাংলা: প্রতিটি অস্পষ্ট শব্দ (big, good, thing) সঠিক ও collocation-উপযোগী শব্দে বদলে দিলে Lexical
        Resource বাড়ে ।

Exercise 2.2 · Context Match
1. eradicate. Why: it means remove completely; alleviate only means ease, so it fails here. বাংলা:
eradicate = সম্পূর্ণ নির্মূল; alleviate = শুধু লাঘব, তাই ভু ল। 2. alleviate. Why: it eases pain that already
exists; eradicate is ruled out by “cannot be cured.” বাংলা: বিদ্যমান কষ্ট লাঘব করা; নির্মূল নয়। 3. mitigate.
Why: mitigate the damage means reduce its severity; the fixed collocation. বাংলা: ক্ষতির তীব্রতা
কমানো; নির্দিষ্ট collocation। 4. soared. Why: soar means a large, rapid rise, matching “dramatically.”
বাংলা: soar = দ্রুত বড় উত্থান, “dramatically”-র সাথে মানানসই। 5. declined. Why: a gradual fall fits
“steadily”; soared would contradict it. বাংলা: “steadily”-র সাথে ধীরে হ্রাস; soared বিপরীত। 6. vital.
Why: means essential; trivial is the opposite and contradicts the sentence. বাংলা: vital = অত্যাবশ্যক;
trivial বিপরীত। 7. revolutionised. Why: a radical, lasting change fits the printing press. বাংলা: আমূল
স্থায়ী পরিবর্তন বোঝায়। 8. trigger. Why: it means set off a harmful event; mitigate would reverse the
meaning. বাংলা: ক্ষতিকর কিছু ঘটানো; mitigate বিপরীত। 9. highlights. Why: to draw attention to a
finding; conceals is the opposite. বাংলা: গুরুত্ব তুলে ধরা; conceals বিপরীত। 10. affluent. Why: means
wealthy; impoverished means the opposite. বাংলা: affluent = ধনী; impoverished বিপরীত। 11.
diminish. Why: to make less; worsen contradicts the benefit of exercise. বাংলা: কমানো; worsen
বিপরীত। 12. reshape. Why: to change significantly; preserve means keep unchanged. বাংলা: বড়
পরিবর্তন; preserve বিপরীত। 13. generated. Why: means produced or caused; resolved means settled,
the opposite. বাংলা: সৃষ্টি করা; resolved বিপরীত। 14. alleviate. Why: to ease suffering; aggravate
means make it worse. বাংলা: কষ্ট লাঘব; aggravate বিপরীত। 15. crucial. Why: means very important;
trivial is the opposite. বাংলা: crucial = অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ; trivial বিপরীত।



Chapter 3: Complete Verb Conjugations and Formal Transitions
Exercise 3.1 · Verb Form and Collocation Drill
1. grown. Why: present perfect needs has + V3; grow is irregular (grew, grown). বাংলা: present
perfect-এ has + V3; grow-এর V3 grown। 2. to rise / rising. Why: continue accepts both the
infinitive and the -ing form. বাংলা: continue-এর পরে to + verb বা -ing দুটোই চলে। 3. on. Why: depend
on is the fixed collocation. বাংলা: depend on। 4. from. Why: benefit from. বাংলা: benefit from। 5.
peaked. Why: simple past for a finished time range. বাংলা: নির্দিষ্ট অতীত সময়ে simple past। 6. risen.
Why: present perfect (has risen); rise is intransitive, so no object. বাংলা: present perfect has risen;
rise intransitive। 7. in. Why: invest in. বাংলা: invest in। 8. eradicated. Why: passive voice needs

was + V3. বাংলা: passive-এ was + V3। 9. undermine. Why: the base form follows the modal may.
বাংলা: modal may-এর পরে base form। 10. focuses. Why: present simple, third person singular (the
report focuses on). বাংলা: third person singular-এ focuses। 11. fallen. Why: past perfect needs had
+ V3; fall is irregular (fell, fallen). বাংলা: past perfect-এ had + V3। 12. to. Why: contribute to. বাংলা:
contribute to। 13. deter … from. Why: base form after can; the structure is deter someone from
doing. বাংলা: can-এর পরে base; deter … from। 14. investing. Why: present perfect continuous
needs has been + V4. বাংলা: present perfect continuous-এ has been + -ing। 15. from. Why: result
from points to a cause; result in points to a consequence. বাংলা: কারণ বোঝাতে result from; ফল বোঝাতে
result in। 16. replacing. Why: present continuous needs are + V4. বাংলা: present continuous-এ
are + -ing। 17. designed … enhance. Why: passive is designed; base form after to. বাংলা: passive is
designed; to-এর পরে base। 18. adapt … to. Why: base form after must; adapt to. বাংলা: must-এর পরে
base; adapt to। 19. risen. Why: present perfect (have risen). বাংলা: present perfect have risen।
20. provided … with. Why: present perfect has provided; provide someone with something. বাংলা:
provide … with।

Exercise 3.2 · Cohesive Device Transformation
Model rewrite:
      Online education has grown enormously in popularity, largely because it is cheaper
      than traditional classes and allows students to study from home. Notwithstanding
      these advantages, it carries certain drawbacks. To begin with, there is far less
      interaction with teachers. Moreover, many learners lack the self-discipline that
      independent study demands; consequently, a significant proportion fail to complete
      their courses. Online education is therefore undeniably useful, yet it cannot fully
      replace the classroom.
  •     Why: because correctly introduces a full clause, while Notwithstanding is correctly
        followed by a noun phrase (these advantages), not a clause; the semicolon before
        consequently joins two related clauses; no device is repeated, so the cohesion is varied
        rather than mechanical.
  •     বাংলা: because-এর পরে পূর্ণ clause; Notwithstanding-এর পরে noun phrase (clause নয়);
        consequently-র আগে semicolon; একই linker বারবার না বসিয়ে বৈচিত্র্য রাখা হয়েছে, যা উচ্চ band-এর
        লক্ষণ।


End of Chapter 7, Part 1. Part 2 consolidates the keys for Chapters 4, 5, and 6.

Exercise 5.1 · Register and Style Sort
The answer is W (appropriate for Task 2) or S (Speaking only). For each S, a formal rewrite is
given.
1. S. These days, many children spend excessive time on their smartphones. (a lot of kids, glued

Chapter 6: Full Workbook and Self-Assessment
Section 1 · Sentence Transformations (Band 9 models)
  1. In the modern era, technology plays an indispensable role in our daily lives.
  2. Many people believe that wealth is the key to happiness.
  3. Pollution poses a serious threat to public health.
  4. The government should allocate greater funding to education.

  5.    A significant proportion of students go abroad in pursuit of well-paid employment.
  6.    Deforestation has a detrimental effect on the environment.
  7.    Children spend excessive time on their phones, which can be detrimental to their
        development.
  8.    An efficient public transport system can substantially reduce urban traffic congestion.
  9.    Examinations place considerable pressure on students.
  10.   Tourism makes a substantial contribution to a nation’s economy.
  11.   Disadvantaged people often lack access to adequate healthcare.
  12.   Social media has fundamentally transformed the way people communicate.
  13.   Although fast food is popular, it gives rise to numerous health problems.
  14.   Large corporations should do more to protect the environment.
  15.   A command of English is crucial for securing well-paid employment.
  16.   The gap between rich and poor continues to widen.
  17.   Excessive television viewing is an unproductive use of children’s time.
  18.   Crime often stems from unemployment and a lack of opportunity.
  19.   Long-standing traditions are gradually disappearing as a result of modern life.
  20.   Renewable energy is a cleaner and more sustainable alternative to fossil fuels.
  •     Why: each transformation replaces an overused word with a precise one, folds two weak
        clauses into one controlled sentence, and swaps a basic linker for an accurate cohesive
        device. That combination of precision and control is what moves a sentence from Band 6
        to Band 9.
  •     বাংলা: প্রতিটি রূপান্তরে অতিব্যবহৃত শব্দ সঠিক শব্দে বদলানো হয়েছে, দুর্বল clause একত্র করে নিয়ন্ত্রিত বাক্য বানানো
        হয়েছে এবং সাধারণ linker সঠিক cohesive device-এ পরিণত হয়েছে; এই নির্ভুলতা ও নিয়ন্ত্রণই Band 6 থেকে
        Band 9-এ নিয়ে যায়।

Section 2 · Essay Rewrites
Full model rewrites for all five essays appear in Chapter 6, Part 1. Compare your version
against the model and check, paragraph by paragraph, whether you applied the following. -
Why (the upgrade checklist): remove first-language slips (I am agree, give importance on,
discuss about); replace overused words (big, good, bad, a lot of, thing) with precise choices;
swap basic linkers (but, so, also) for cohesive devices (Nevertheless, Consequently,
Furthermore); and add at least one formal collocation per paragraph (reap the benefits, strike a
balance, pose a serious threat to). - বাংলা: L1 ভু ল সরান (I am agree, discuss about); অতিব্যবহৃত শব্দ সঠিক
শব্দে বদলান; সাধারণ linker-এর বদলে cohesive device দিন; প্রতিটি অনুচ্ছেদে অন্তত একটি আনুষ্ঠানিক collocation
যোগ করুন। পূর্ণ মডেল রচনা Chapter 6, Part 1-এ আছে।
